newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi sets up water, power privatisation board.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi sets up water, power privatisation board.

text.p: Abu Dhabi emirate has set up a committee to oversee the privatisation of its water and electricity services, the official WAM news agency reported.
In a report late on Tuesday it said the committee, headed by Abu Dhabi Planning Department Chairman Musallam al-Qubaisi, had appointed consultants to study the feasibility of privatisation.
Like its Gulf neighbours, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), whose capital is Abu Dhabi, wants to reduce reliance on the dominant public sector and give private investors a bigger role.
WAM said the water and electricity sector had taken the lion's share of UAE investment in the past few years, accounting for over seven billion dirhams ($1.9 billion) in three years.
"The government is expected to save some 10 billion dirhams by the year 2000 if the water and electricity sector was sold off," WAM said.

It said water consumption in the UAE, where the population is growing at around four percent annually, was expected to rise to almost 606 million gallons (2.7 billion litres) a day by the year 2015 from a current 232.5 million.
Last year the UAE raised power rates by 33 percent, but electricity and water are still heavily subsidised.
Earlier this month Abu Dhabi Water and Electricity director general Hassan al-Nassay said the cost of producing 1,000 gallons (4,545 litres) of water was 28-30 dirhams (around $8).
In July the department raised water charges to 10 dirhams per 1,000 gallons from seven dirhams.
